name: Fesoterodine versus tolterodine ER
question: Does fesoterodine 8 mg reduce urgency urinary incontinence more than tolterodine ER 4 mg or placebo in adults with overactive bladder?

arms.label: Fesoterodine 8 mg daily after a 4 mg lead-in

design.population: 1,712 randomized adults; eligibility required overactive bladder symptoms for at least 3 months, at least 8 voids and at least 1 urgency urinary incontinence episode per 24 hours in baseline 3-day diaries; 1,590 entered the full efficacy analysis set.
design.description: Double-blind, double-dummy, placebo-controlled randomized trial; arm counts are the treated safety set (1,697 total).
design.locator: Full text, Patients and Methods, p 59; Results and Fig. 2, pp 60–61

verdictNote: The prespecified UUI comparison met significance; diary dryness was analyzed post hoc.
takeaway: In a 12-week randomized trial, fesoterodine 8 mg reduced daily urgency urinary incontinence episodes by 1.72 versus 1.61 with tolterodine ER 4 mg (P = 0.017) and 1.46 with placebo (P < 0.001); dry mouth was more frequent with fesoterodine.

reports.label: 12-week head-to-head trial
reports.citation: Herschorn S, Swift S, Guan Z, et al. "Comparison of fesoterodine and tolterodine extended release for the treatment of overactive bladder: a head-to-head placebo-controlled trial." *BJU Int.* 2010;105(1):58-66. doi:10.1111/j.1464-410X.2009.09086.x
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Patients and Methods, p 59

results.measure: Winsorized mean change from baseline to week 12 in episodes per 24 hours, fesoterodine versus tolterodine ER
results.note: Difference calculated from rounded Figure 3A arm values; full analysis set with UUI at baseline; Van Elteren test; no confidence interval reported.
results.locator: Full text, Fig. 3A, p 63; Results, p 61

results.measure: Winsorized mean change from baseline to week 12 in episodes per 24 hours, fesoterodine versus placebo
results.note: Difference calculated from rounded Figure 3A arm values; full analysis set with UUI at baseline; Van Elteren test; no confidence interval reported.
results.locator: Full text, Fig. 3A, p 63; Results, p 61

results.measure: No UUI episodes at week 12 among patients with at least one at baseline; post hoc analysis
results.note: Post hoc analysis; participants with no baseline UUI were excluded.

results.measure: Least-squares mean change from baseline to week 12, mL per void
results.note: Difference calculated from rounded Figure 3B arm values; no confidence interval reported.
results.locator: Full text, Fig. 3B, p 63; Results, p 61

results.measure: Least-squares mean change from baseline to week 12, fesoterodine versus tolterodine ER
results.note: Fesoterodine–tolterodine comparison did not meet the prespecified two-sided 5% threshold.
